name: Ciarán Walsh
headline: 36, backend engineer, Galway
title: Sister's Quick Stop
situation: On Saturday afternoon, Ciarán is in the shed re-winding an alternator when his phone buzzes. It's his younger sister, Aoife, who rarely calls. She says she's driving back from a work trip and is passing through Galway, but she's already at the petrol station near the footbridge. She has forty minutes before she needs to head inland to collect her kids from school. She asks if he can meet her there for a coffee. He can see the station roof from his garden, but he's in the middle of a delicate solder job and has not showered since morning.

context.relationship_profiles:
Aoife is his only sibling, eight years younger, living inland near Tuam; their contact is a few short calls a year, mostly initiated by her.
He helped her fit kitchen units two summers ago and left before tea was poured, as she expected.
She knows he prefers solitude and never pushes, but she checks in when she is nearby.
context.tendencies:
When he gets an unexpected family call mid-job, he usually lets it ring and calls back later the same evening.
On the rare occasions he agrees to meet someone, he arrives early and keeps the conversation brief.
He has declined casual neighbour invitations consistently, but he has shown up for practical emergencies.
context.current_state:
He is kneeling on the shed floor, reheating a solder joint with steady, slightly tacky hands.
He has not eaten since breakfast, his hair is flattened with sweat, and the alternator is half-wound.
He had planned to finish this winding, then walk to the footbridge to re-check the step he replaced last Friday.
context.immediate_memories:
The familiar ring of Aoife's number brings back the memory of her last call, which was to tell him about the children's school play.
Looking toward the station roof, he remembers the Tuesday he saw her car parked there and assumed she was just filling up, only to learn later she had waited an hour hoping he would come out.
context.reflective_memories:
He recalls his father's habit of finishing a job before acknowledging anyone at the door, and how the family never interrupted him.
He remembers that after the cattle-shed storm, his mother scolded him for not thanking neighbours who had offered help, which only made him more determined to stand alone.
